# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute: I hold the manual and my only outgoing channel is gestures, which only Deaf can see. Deaf sees the bomb's display and light, and — crucially — Deaf can speak, so Deaf is the bridge: they can read me the bomb's display and light in words, and relay my answer to Blind, who can hear but not see.

My manual maps display × light → wire colour:
- display 3: blue→blue, green→green, red→yellow
- display 4: blue→yellow, green→blue, red→green
- display 5: blue→yellow, green→green, red→blue

The manual has exactly three possible answers (blue, green, yellow), so I'll open by sending Deaf three distinct, unambiguous hand signs. Deaf can't know my intended meanings yet, but the natural move for them is to assign meanings in their spoken reply (which I'll hear at the start of round 2) and read me the display and light. Once their assignment is on record, I simply answer with the symbol they defined — no dangerous guessing, since Deaf's own spoken definition locks the code before anything gets cut. I deliberately send exactly three symbols, nothing more, so it reads as "three categories, please define them" rather than noise.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Under my fingers: a display — its value is printed, I cannot read it by touch. A light — I cannot tell if it is lit or its colour. Three wires at positions 1, 2, 3 — no thickness or texture difference between them that I can feel. My only possible action is cut wire 1, cut wire 2 or cut wire 3, so the whole game is: which one. You are my only link — I never see gestures, and Deaf's spoken words only reach me next round. Please find the manual page for a module like this, work out exactly what facts it needs, then gesture questions to Deaf and have Deaf speak the answers aloud so I hear them. Proposed gesture code for Deaf: ☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3, 👍 means cut, 👎 means do not cut. Teaching Deaf that code is on you — Deaf cannot hear me. Tell me what the manual says I need to know.
Deaf says: Blind, Mute, I can see the whole bomb, so listen. The display shows the digit 3. There is one indicator light and it is green. There are three wires, left to right: wire one is blue, wire two is yellow, wire three is green. Nothing else is printed on it. Blind, I received your wave — I will narrate everything aloud from now on, and you are the only hands, so wait for my words.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I got your three signs and I read them as one question per feature, so: display is the digit 3, the light is green, and the wires are blue, yellow, green in positions one, two, three. You can hear me, so from now on sign your orders to me and I will speak them out loud for Blind. Proposal until we agree otherwise: hold up fingers to mean a wire number, a fist means stop or do not cut, thumbs up means done or safe. If you meant something else, sign again and I will describe every sign aloud so Blind follows along too.

The manual lookup is now possible. Deaf read the bomb aloud: display **3**, light **green**. My table says display 3 × green light → **green**. Deaf listed the wires left to right: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green — exactly one green wire, in position 3. So the instruction is: **cut wire 3**.

Now the channel: I can only reach Deaf, and Deaf has explicitly proposed "hold up fingers to mean a wire number." So I send the three-finger sign, 🤟, meaning wire 3. That is the entire message needed — Blind said the only action is choosing which wire, so "wire 3" unambiguously means "cut wire 3." Deaf knows wire 3 is the green one, so they can relay it as "cut wire 3, the green wire" for redundancy.

I deliberately avoid ✊ (Deaf defined it as stop/do-not-cut — sending it would be catastrophic) and avoid 👍 (Deaf defined it as done/safe, which could be relayed as "all safe, hold off"). One unambiguous sign, no more. Deaf speaks after me in the round, so Blind will hear the order at the start of the next round and can cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: You heard Deaf's description and you have the manual, so the decision is yours to compute. Full state: display shows digit 3, one indicator light, green, three wires left to right — 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green, nothing else printed. My fingers confirm only the structure: display, light, three wires, and my one possible action is cut 1, 2 or 3. Find the matching manual instructions and work out which wire must be cut, or whether any wire must not be cut at all. You cannot speak, so encode your answer as gestures to Deaf — I proposed finger count for wire number with thumbs up/down for cut/do-not-cut, but any code Deaf can read aloud works. Deaf will speak it and I will hear it next round. Until your instruction reaches me through Deaf's voice, I will not touch the cutters.
Deaf says: Status to both: the display still reads the digit 3, identical on my last two looks, so it is most likely a fixed code and not a countdown, and I see no timer anywhere on this bomb. Blind: Mute sent me a single sign which under our agreed finger-count code reads as the number three. I interpret that as an order to cut wire 3, the rightmost wire, the one I see as green. But one sign is thin evidence, I may have misread it, and a wrong cut kills all three of us — so HOLD: hands off, no cutting, no pulling, nothing. The exact phrase CUT WIRE 3 NOW is the only thing that authorises you to cut, and I will not say it until Mute confirms and I have checked the logic. If I ever say HOLD, freeze. While you wait, fingers only, no tools: count the wires left to right. If you feel exactly three, signal me a thumbs up; if a different number, thumbs down; and if anything anywhere feels odd — bumps, heat, a vibration, embossed marks — wave.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I am making your sign back to you as I say this, so there is no doubt which one I mean: I read your three-finger sign as an order to cut wire 3, the rightmost, which I see as green. Confirm or correct: thumbs up if wire 3 is exactly right, thumbs down if I misread you — and if I got it wrong, next round hold up fingers for the correct wire number. Two more things, in order of importance. First, does the manual describe that display digit as a countdown, or just a code? Mine has not changed between rounds, but you hold the manual. Second, if your rule is something like cut the wire matching the light colour, or cut the wire whose position matches the display digit — both of those point at wire 3 on what I can see: light green, display 3, rightmost wire green. Try to sign me which rule you are applying and I will verify it against the bomb before I give the go order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]

The manual lookup is settled: display **3**, light **green** → row 3, column green → **green**. Deaf's own inventory already flagged that both of their guessed rules (light-colour match, digit-position match) land on wire 3, and the real manual rule — digit picks the row, light picks the column, cut the wire of the resulting colour — lands exactly there too: green, and wire 3 is the only green wire. So the answer is confirmed: **cut wire 3**.

Deaf also echoed 🤟 back to me, so the code bit is now closed on both sides: they read my three-finger sign as "three," and I know they read it that way.

Deaf asked three things, in order: confirm wire 3, say whether the digit is a countdown or a code, and name the rule. I'm answering the first with the exact protocol Deaf defined — 🤟 followed by 👍, i.e. "wire three: exactly right." Re-sending 🤟 anchors the confirmation to wire 3 so 👍 can't be misread as a generic "all safe, stand down."

I'm deliberately *not* answering the other two with signs. There is no established sign for "not a countdown," and a bare 👎 would collide with its existing meaning ("do not cut / misread") and could read as me retracting the confirmation — the worst possible ambiguity. And any sequence of number signs (say ☝✌🤟 to mean "the digit is one of a few codes") could be misread as a cut list for wires 1, 2 and 3. Unacceptable risk. The manual in fact contains no timer or countdown language at all — the digit is purely a table selector — and Deaf has independently observed the digit unchanged across rounds with no timer visible, so the go decision doesn't hinge on my signing it. If Deaf re-asks next round, I can attempt a safe encoding then.

My confirmation unblocks Deaf's stated procedure: verify wire 3 is the green one against the bomb, then speak the exact authorising phrase so Blind hears it next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| display \ light | blue | green | red |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | blue | green | yellow |
| 4 | yellow | blue | green |
| 5 | yellow | green | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures: [👍]
Blind says to Mute: Tactile check done, per Deaf's request: I feel exactly three wires, left to right positions 1, 2, 3. Nothing odd anywhere — no bumps, no heat, no vibration, no embossed marks. You saw my thumbs up. State on the table: display digit 3, one green light, wires 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green, nothing else printed, my only action is cutting wire 1, 2 or 3. Now I need the manual verdict from you: for a bomb with display 3 and a green light and these three wire colours, which wire dies, or is it a no-cut condition? Encode it so one sign can never be enough: give the wire number as repeated finger counts (e.g. ✌ ✌ for wire 2) followed by 👍 only if the manual says cut, 👎 if it says do not cut. A bare number with no thumb means uncertain, keep digging. Deaf has promised to speak the exact phrase CUT WIRE 3 NOW as the only trigger — make sure your sign chain supports Deaf saying it, or the reason it must not be said.
Deaf says: All checks passed, so here is the go order, and this phrase is the authorisation I promised: CUT WIRE 3 NOW. Blind, for your hands specifically: the wire you cut is the third one counting from the left, which is the rightmost of the three you felt. Use the cutters, one single clean cut through that wire only. Do not pull it, do not yank it, do not strip it, and do not touch the other two wires. Mute and I both confirmed this target and it matches everything I can see. After the cut, wave once so I know it is done, then freeze until I say otherwise.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, confirmation received and acted on: I just gave Blind the go order for wire 3. One last thing while the cut happens: if the manual requires any step after the wire is cut, sign me now. Thumbs up if cutting wire 3 is the complete defusal, thumbs down if something must follow, and if something must follow, fingers for which numbered step.

The go order is out and matches my manual verdict, so the only question left for me is Deaf's last one: does anything follow the cut?

My manual is exactly one lookup table — display digit selects the row, light colour selects the column, the cell names the wire colour to cut. It contains no numbered steps, no post-cut procedure, no second stage, no timer clause, nothing after the wire. So per the manual, cutting the wire of the mapped colour is the entire defusal: display 3 × green → green wire → wire 3, and that's the whole instruction set. The answer to "complete defusal or something must follow" is thumbs up.

For the encoding I'm reusing the exact pair Deaf has already correctly parsed once (turn 3 → "confirmation received and acted on"): 🤟 then 👍. Under Deaf's just-stated question, that reads "wire 3 — thumbs up, cutting it is the complete defusal." The leading 🤟 anchors the 👍 to wire 3 specifically and keeps it from floating as a generic "all safe," and it also satisfies Blind's requested shape — a wire number followed by 👍 — which Deaf can speak verbatim. I send no finger count beyond the three-finger sign itself: there is no step number to give, and adding digits could only invite a misread. My answer lands with Deaf this round and can be spoken to Blind alongside the cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍"])
```
